units.title: Spinal nerves
units.summary: Spinal Nerves ⚫ Total 31 pairs of spinal nerves ⚫ Exit & enter the spinal cord at the various vertebral levels ⚫ Cervical region: 8 pairs ⚫ Thoracic region: 12 pairs ⚫ Lumbar region: 5 pairs ⚫ Sacral region: 5 pairs ⚫ Coccygeal region: 1 pair Spinal Nerves ⚫ Sensoryneurons:the nerves that entering the spinal cord on the dorsal root (posterior) ⚫ Transmit information into the system from the muscle ⚫ Afferent pathway – carries all incoming information ⚫ Motorneurons: the nerves that exiting on the ventralroot (anterior) of the spinal cord ⚫ Carry impulses away from the system to the muscle ⚫ Efferent pathway – carries all outgoing information ⚫ Both dorsal & ventral roots join together as spinal nervesas they exit the spinal cord Spinal Nerves ⚫ Area of the body supplied by the spinal nerves Spinal nerve Area supplied Cervical: 8 pairs Head, neck, shoulders, arms, hands, diaphragm Thoracic: 12 pairs Chest, some back muscles, parts of abdomen Lumbar: 5 pairs Lower parts of abdomen & back, buttocks, parts of the external genital organs, parts of the legs Sacral: 5 pairs Thigh, lower parts of legs, feet, most of the external genital organs, area around the anus
summary_sentences: Spinal Nerves ⚫ Total 31 pairs of spinal nerves ⚫ Exit & enter the spinal cord at the various vertebral levels ⚫ Cervical region: 8 pairs ⚫ Thoracic region: 12 pairs ⚫ Lumbar region: 5 pairs ⚫ Sacral region: 5 pairs ⚫ Coccygeal region: 1 pair

units.title: Motor units
units.summary: Motor Unit ⚫ Skeletal muscle is organized into functional groups called motor units. ⚫ Motorunit: ⚫ consists of a group of muscle fibers that are innervated by the same motorneuron ⚫ From a few muscle fibers or up to 2000 muscle fibers ⚫ When a motor neuron is stimulated enough to cause a contraction, all muscle fibers innervated by that motor neuron contract ⚫ Action potential: the signal to contract that is transmitted from the motor neuron to the muscle ⚫ The action potential from a motor neuron reaches a muscle fiber at motorend plate (neuromuscular junction) Motor Unit ⚫ The motor unit consists of a motor neuron & all of the muscle fibers innervated by that neuron. ⚫ The motor neurons exit the anterior side of the spinal cord and branch out, terminating on the muscle fibers.
summary_sentences: Motor Unit ⚫ Skeletal muscle is organized into functional groups called motor units.

⚫ Motorunit: ⚫ consists of a group of muscle fibers that are innervated by the same motorneuron ⚫ From a few muscle fibers or up to 2000 muscle fibers ⚫ When a motor neuron is stimulated enough to cause a contraction, all muscle fibers innervated by that motor neuron contract ⚫ Action potential: the signal to contract that is transmitted from the motor neuron to the muscle ⚫ The action potential from a motor neuron reaches a muscle fiber at motorend plate (neuromuscular junction)
Motor Unit ⚫ The motor unit consists of a motor neuron & all of the muscle fibers innervated by that neuron.
⚫ The motor neurons exit the anterior side of the spinal cord and branch out, terminating on the muscle fibers.

units.title: Sensory receptors, reflexes, and proprioceptors
units.summary: Sensory Receptors ⚫ The body requires an input system to provide feedbackon the condition & changing characteristics of the musculoskeletal system and other body tissues, such as skin ⚫ Sensors collect the following information: ⚫ Stretch in the muscle ⚫ Heat / pressure on the muscle ⚫ Tension in the muscle ⚫ Pain in the extremity Sensory Receptors ⚫ These sensors send information to the spinal cord ⚫ Information is processed & used by the central nervous system in the adjustment / initiation of motor output to the muscles ⚫ These sensors are connected to the spinal cord via sensory neurons ⚫ When a sensory neuron brings information into the spinal cord and initiates a motor response, it is termed a reflex Reflex ⚫ Asimple reflex arc ⚫ Sensory information from receptors is sent into the spinal cord ➢ Motor response is sent out to the extremities ➢ e.g. Proprioceptors ⚫ Proprioceptors ⚫ Mainsensory receptors in the musculoskeletal system ⚫ transform mechanical distortion in the muscle into the nerve impulses that enter the spinal cord & stimulate a motor response ⚫ Examples: ⚫ Muscle spindle: found in belly of the muscle; responds to the change in muscle length or velocity of a muscle stretch ⚫ Golgi tendonorgan(GTO): found in muscle-tendon junction; responds to tension in the muscle
summary_sentences: Sensory Receptors ⚫ The body requires an input system to provide feedbackon the condition & changing characteristics of the musculoskeletal system and other body tissues, such as skin ⚫ Sensors collect the following information: ⚫ Stretch in the muscle ⚫ Heat / pressure on the muscle ⚫ Tension in the muscle ⚫ Pain in the extremity
